Termite Control Cost: What to Expect in Kansas (2024)

By Shaw's Pest Control  ·  Wichita, KS

How Much Does Termite Control Cost? A Transparent Price Breakdown

If you're researching termite control cost, you've likely found evidence of termites or you're buying a home that needs treatment. Either way, you want a straight answer on pricing—not a runaround.

The honest answer: termite treatment typically costs between $500 and $3,500, depending on your home's size, the treatment method used, and the severity of the infestation. Here in Wichita and the surrounding Kansas communities we serve, most homeowners pay between $1,200 and $2,000 for comprehensive termite control. At Shaw's Pest Control, we've been protecting Kansas homes since 1987 with upfront pricing and no-pressure consultations backed by our Master Tech Certification and three state certifications.

This guide breaks down exactly what affects termite control cost, the difference between treatment types, and what you should expect to pay for real, lasting protection.

What Determines Termite Control Cost?

The price you'll pay for termite treatment isn't arbitrary—it's based on specific factors related to your property and the treatment method required.

Home size is the primary cost driver. Treatment is typically priced per linear foot of your home's foundation. A 1,500-square-foot home with 150 linear feet of foundation will cost less than a 3,000-square-foot home with 250 linear feet. Most companies charge between $3 and $16 per linear foot depending on the treatment type.

Infestation severity matters significantly. An active infestation with visible damage requires more extensive treatment than preventative measures. If termites have compromised structural wood, you'll need both pest control and potential repairs, which adds to the total investment.

Treatment method creates the widest price variation. Liquid barrier treatments using termiticides typically run $1,500–$3,500 for initial application. Bait station systems like the Advance Termite Bait System we use at Shaw's range from $1,200–$2,500 for installation and monitoring. Each approach has distinct advantages, which we'll cover next.

Accessibility around your home's foundation also affects pricing. Homes with landscaping, concrete patios, or crawl spaces that are difficult to access require additional labor, which can increase costs by 10–30%.

Liquid Treatment vs. Bait Systems: Cost and Effectiveness

Understanding the two primary termite control methods helps you make an informed decision about which investment makes sense for your home.

Liquid barrier treatments create a chemical barrier in the soil around your home's foundation. Exterminators drill into concrete slabs or trench around the foundation to apply liquid termiticide. This method typically costs $1,500–$3,500 depending on home size and the amount of product required. The treatment is immediately effective at killing termites that contact the treated soil, and it typically lasts 5–10 years. However, it requires drilling, trenching, and significant chemical application.

Bait station systems take a different approach. Stations are installed around your property's perimeter at 10–15 foot intervals. These stations contain wood monitoring devices that attract termites. Once termite activity is detected, the wood is replaced with bait that termites carry back to the colony, eliminating it at the source. Initial installation typically costs $1,200–$2,500, with annual monitoring fees of $300–$500.

At Shaw's Pest Control, we exclusively use the Advance Termite Bait System for several reasons. It's less invasive—no drilling through your foundation. It's targeted—the bait eliminates the entire colony rather than creating a chemical perimeter. And it's environmentally conscious, using minimal product only where termites are actively feeding. For most Wichita-area homes, our complete Advance system installation runs $1,400–$2,200 depending on property size, with annual monitoring included in our service agreements.

The choice often comes down to your priorities: immediate barrier protection with liquid treatment, or colony elimination with monitoring through bait systems.

What About Termite Inspection Costs?

Before treatment, you need an inspection—and understanding inspection pricing prevents surprises.

Most professional termite inspections cost $75–150 as a standalone service. However, many pest control companies waive the inspection fee if you proceed with treatment. At Shaw's, we offer free termite inspections because we'd rather you make an informed decision than face a surprise fee.

A proper inspection takes 45–90 minutes and includes examination of your home's foundation, crawl space, basement, attic, and any areas with moisture issues or wood-to-soil contact. The inspector looks for mud tubes, damaged wood, discarded wings, and termite droppings. You'll receive a written report detailing any findings and recommended treatment.

If you're buying a home, lenders often require a termite inspection as part of closing. These inspections typically cost $100–200 and follow specific reporting standards. If active termites are found, treatment becomes a condition of sale—and understanding termite control in Wichita pricing helps you negotiate who covers the cost.

Wood-destroying insect reports (WDI reports) are slightly more comprehensive than standard inspections and may cost $125–200. These reports document all wood-destroying pests, not just termites, and are often required for VA and FHA loans.

Don't skip the inspection to save money. A $100 inspection can reveal a $5,000 problem before it becomes a $15,000 structural disaster.

Termite Control Cost in the Wichita Area

Wichita's climate—with our hot summers and temperature swings—creates ideal conditions for subterranean termites, the most common type in Kansas. Termites remain active in our area from early spring through late fall, with swarms typically appearing in March and April when the weather warms.

Local termite control pricing in Wichita, Derby, El Dorado, and surrounding communities tends to fall in the mid-range nationally. You're not paying premium coastal pricing, but Kansas isn't a low-cost market either. Expect professional treatment to cost $1,200–$2,500 for most residential properties.

One advantage of working with a local company like Shaw's: we understand Kansas construction methods, soil conditions, and termite behavior patterns specific to our region. We've protected homes throughout Sedgwick and Butler counties for over 35 years, and that experience means efficient treatment without unnecessary upselling.

If you own property in communities like El Dorado, where many homes feature pier-and-beam construction, bait systems often work particularly well because they don't require drilling through foundation slabs. Location-specific factors like these affect both treatment approach and final cost.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does termite treatment cost on average?

Termite treatment costs between $500 and $3,500 for most homes, with the national average around $1,500. Liquid barrier treatments typically run $1,500–$3,500, while bait station systems cost $1,200–$2,500 for installation. Annual monitoring for bait systems adds $300–$500. Your final cost depends on home size, treatment method, infestation severity, and regional pricing variations.

Is termite control a one-time cost or ongoing expense?

Termite control involves both initial treatment and ongoing monitoring. Liquid treatments last 5–10 years before reapplication, making them closer to a one-time expense with occasional retreatment. Bait systems require annual monitoring at $300–$500 per year to remain effective. Most companies, including Shaw's Pest Control, offer service agreements that include annual inspections and monitoring to catch problems early.

What's the difference between termite prevention and treatment costs?

Preventative termite control costs $500–$1,500 and involves installing bait stations or applying barrier treatments before an infestation occurs. Active infestation treatment costs $1,200–$3,500 because it requires more extensive product application and often involves treating structural damage areas. Prevention is significantly cheaper than treating an established colony, which is why many homeowners invest in monitoring systems.

Does homeowners insurance cover termite control cost?

Homeowners insurance typically does not cover termite control or termite damage because it's considered preventable maintenance, similar to routine pest control. Most policies specifically exclude insect damage unless it results from a covered peril. However, some insurance companies offer separate termite damage endorsements for an additional premium. Your best protection is regular inspection and preventative treatment.

How often do you need to pay for termite control?

With liquid barrier treatments, retreatment is needed every 5–10 years depending on the product used and soil conditions. Bait systems require annual monitoring visits at $300–$500 per year. At Shaw's Pest Control, our service agreements include quarterly pest control with annual termite monitoring, spreading the cost throughout the year rather than facing a large one-time expense.

Can I treat termites myself to save money?

DIY termite treatment products cost $50–300 but rarely eliminate an established colony. Over-the-counter termiticides lack the concentration of professional products, and improper application often drives termites deeper into your home rather than eliminating them. Most homeowners who attempt DIY treatment end up paying for professional service anyway—after additional damage has occurred. Given that termites cause $5 billion in U.S. property damage annually, professional treatment is a worthwhile investment.
